content.text: I'll check the connected providers and the local data inventory first.
The local database has step records from two providers. I'll pull both for October 1–3 to compare them.

Here's what's stored locally for October 1–3, 2026. Only steps have data for these dates.

**Daily steps**

| Date | Google | Fitbit | Used in totals |
|---|---|---|---|
| Oct 1 | 1,000 | 9,000 | Google (1,000) |
| Oct 2 | 2,000 | no record | Google (2,000) |
| Oct 3 | 3,000 | no record | Google (3,000) |
| **Total** | **6,000** | 9,000 (Oct 1 only) | **6,000** |

**Provider selection**
- I used Google as the single source for all three days. It is the only provider with a complete set of records for the period, so one source gives a consistent series.
- Fitbit has only Oct 1, so using it would mean mixing sources within the period.
- Each provider's records are one value per day, so I didn't add providers together.

**Avoiding double-counting**
- Oct 1 has two values for the same day and metric. Adding them (10,000) would double-count the day. Only one value per day should be used.
- The gap on Oct 1 is large (1,000 vs. 9,000). The local data can't tell me which figure is accurate. The two providers may count steps differently, or one of the imported values may be wrong. Check the Oct 1 values in each app before relying on that day.

**Limitations**
- Neither provider currently has a verified connection, so these figures come from previously imported local records and not from a live check.
- The Fitbit legacy Web API is scheduled to shut down on 2026-10-30, so Fitbit syncing may stop working after that date.
- No sleep, heart rate, exercise, or other categories are stored for these dates, so I can't summarize them.
